newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-DALY RETURNS, TRIM AND SOBER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DALY RETURNS, TRIM AND SOBER.

text.p: A healthy-looking John Daly, fresh from eight weeks of alcoholism treatment, returned Tuesday to the PGA Tour some 32 pounds (14.5 kg) slimmer to practice for this week's Memorial Tournament.

"I don't have a lot of expectations this week, I just want to get back into the rhythm, the basics of my game," said Daly, who added he had not played much golf during his two months as an outpatient at the Betty Ford Centre.
"(Staying sober) is always going to be the most important thing in my life, with golf second, because I won't be able to play golf unless I take care of my problems day to day."

The long-hitting Daly, who exploded onto the international scene by winning the 1991 PGA Championship after joining the field as a last-minute alternate, hit rock bottom at the Players Championship in March.

On the evening of March 27, following the first round of play, Daly went on a drinking binge. After a raucous night at a bar, Daly did $1,000 in damage to his hotel room, according to police reports, and caused his wife Paulette to make frantic calls to Daly's agent and to his friend Fuzzy Zoeller.
When it was over, Daly woke up in a hospital, and Paulette had decided to end their two-year marriage.
"They tell you not to remember too much of your past, to just forgive yourself for it. But I want to remember that night for the rest of my life, how bad it really was," Daly said Tuesday.

"When I woke up, my agents were there, my caddy and my best friend Donnie (Crabtree) were there, and I saw the sadness in their eyes. I could just picture how bad I looked, and that's what's going to keep me going, get me through each day, because I don't want to go back there."
Since that night Paulette has refused to speak to Daly, though he has been able to see their two-year-old daughter, Sierra, named after the alchohol rehab centre Daly was forced to enter in 1993.
Daly, 31, is attempting to keep himself straight now with support groups everywhere he goes, and following a 12-step programme.
His first attempt at sobriety, a two and a half year period during which Daly was able to win in Atlanta and the 1995 British Open but managed up just one other top 10 finish, ended last summer.
"I skipped right from step one to 12 the first time. I just said that I quit, which is the stupidest thing I could have ever said," admitted Daly.

"I know now that it is day to day. It's tough. If I go out with the guys to eat, I will kindly ask that they please not drink in front of me, and I just really can't go to cocktail parties anymore. I don't want to put myself in that position anymore."
Daly, who was also dropped by his long-time club manufacturer, Wilson, has since signed with Callaway, his contract stipulating that Daly refrain from his two addictions of drinking and gambling.
"Keep it straight, John" is the catchphrase from the new Callaway ads touting Daly, a phrase Daly suggested himself.
